rows.verified: Employers must provide adequate ventilation in enclosed workplace areas.
Ventilation brings in fresh outside air and removes stale, hot, humid or polluted indoor air.
Employers should assess workplaces to identify poorly ventilated areas.
Employers should select actions suited to the building and workplace to improve ventilation.
Natural ventilation can use doors, windows, trickle vents, air bricks or grilles.
Mechanical ventilation uses fans and may use ducts to supply clean air or extract stale air.
Workplaces may use natural ventilation, mechanical ventilation or a mixture of both.
Regulation 6 of the Workplace Health, Safety and Welfare Regulations requires sufficient fresh or purified air in enclosed workplaces.
Ventilation risk depends on room use, occupancy, building design, outdoor-air supply, pollutants, heat, maintenance and operating conditions.
HSE ventilation evidence is building-, room-, occupancy-, system-, pollutant- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level health probability.
HSE guidance addresses prevention of work-related contact dermatitis and contact urticaria.
Employers and employee representatives can use the guidance to identify occupations and tasks with increased skin risk.
Employers should identify skin hazards and assess who may be exposed and how.
Preventive controls should reduce or avoid skin contact with hazardous substances where reasonably practicable.
Suitable gloves and protective clothing may be needed when exposure cannot be adequately prevented by other controls.
Skin-care arrangements can include appropriate washing, drying and moisturising facilities.
Workers should receive information and training about skin hazards, controls and early signs of disease.
Health surveillance may be appropriate where workers remain at risk of occupational dermatitis.
Dermatitis risk depends on substance, concentration, wet work, contact duration, glove use, skin condition, hygiene and individual susceptibility.
HSE dermatitis evidence is substance-, task-, workplace-, control-, worker- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level disease probability.
